high: Gate C/D failure remains: from the declared initial order, removing any one of the five optional acts and immediately submitting succeeds without opening the changeover document, reordering anything, or understanding setup grouping. Thus the first-play solution is still content-independent; the player can click any visible × once and win.
medium: Act cards still show only name and runtime, not the assigned band/light/none setup type. Even a player who opens the changeover document must infer each act's hidden category from its name or experimentally inspect transition values.

The new QA check does not verify the component's actual initial state. It computes the schedule for ACTS.map(...) but never imports, renders, or inspects TimetableGame's useState initializer, so it would continue passing if the component later initialized a different lineup.
low: Pinned-boundary controls remain misleadingly enabled: opening's down button, ending's up button, and optional-act controls directed into a pinned boundary call move(), which silently rejects them.

overAttempts is cumulative across lineup edits. This is not currently correctness-breaking, but after one failed submission, even a substantially revised lineup receives the second-stage hint on its next failure rather than restarting the hint sequence.

recommended_actions: Rebalance the initial order and timing so at least some arbitrary first cuts still overflow and successful completion requires a changeover-aware reorder, or require an explicit scheduling objective that cannot be satisfied by any single blind deletion.
Add visible, neutral setup-type labels/icons to each act so the rule document provides actionable information rather than requiring name-based inference.

Extend the QA harness with a component-level assertion of the actual initial lineup and a first-play exploit check that rejects the strategy 'remove each optional act in turn without reordering; every result passes.'
Disable move buttons whenever their requested destination is a pinned opening/ending slot.
Consider resetting overAttempts when the lineup changes if each substantially revised schedule should receive the first-stage feedback before escalation.
